name: Government of Germany
detail: Only Development Minister Svenja Schulze co-signed the April 2024 global billionaire levy article; the German government as a whole was against a global billionaire tax at the 2024 G20. One ministry is not the government.

name: The G20 states that signed the Rio leaders' declaration (November 2024)
detail: The declaration says the signatories will seek "to ensure that ultra-high-net-worth individuals are effectively taxed" without naming a tax on wealth: close to the "tax the rich" wording that does not count on its own.

name: Government of Uruguay
detail: President Orsi (Aug 2025): "no encontramos la necesidad de generar más impuestos"; he does not plan a tax on the richest 1%, which the PIT-CNT union centre asked for. The government applies only the OECD global minimum tax on multinationals.

name: Brazil's written positions in the UN tax convention negotiations (2026)
detail: Brazil asks for measures against tax avoidance and evasion by high-net-worth individuals and for "effective taxation" judged by the overall progressivity of the tax system: not a tax on the stock of wealth. Brazil is already recorded on other evidence.

name: Government of Brazil
detail: Removed on review: a G20 communiqué that only names the Zucman blueprint, a 2025 Spain-Brazil text that says the super-rich should be 'taxed more efficiently according to their wealth', and two General Assembly speeches that ask for 'proportional' or 'minimal global' taxation, none of them naming a wealth tax.

name: Government of Spain
detail: Removed on review: the 2025 Spain-Brazil text and UN news report say only that the super-rich should contribute more or be taxed more efficiently, without naming a wealth tax.

name: Government of Norway
detail: Removed on review: a raised threshold for the existing wealth tax is a change to it, not a statement of support.
